title: Design the relative field-extension abstraction and field identity
description:
Author the design document fixing the canonical relative finite-field extension abstraction for gf2-core and the stable algebraic field identity shared by serialization validation and automatic field selection.

## Background

gf2-core has concrete extension configurations (`ExtConfig` binomial towers, runtime `Gf2mField`) but no canonical public relationship expressing that one field extends another: no relative degree, checked membership, restriction, or relative Frobenius across two field types. Compile-time and runtime quotient fields will coexist, so the design must fix one identity and conversion semantics between them. Field identity is algebraic — characteristic, base tower, modulus, basis semantics — and is distinct from the element wire representation, which serialized headers version separately.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A design document in the epic's dev/active directory defines the extension trait surface (embedding, checked membership and restriction, relative degree, relative Frobenius, field-order relationships, validation certificates), citing the existing types it must cover.
- [hard] REQ-02: The document fixes the algebraic field-identity representation, its distinctness from element wire representation, and the equivalence/conversion semantics between compile-time and runtime forms of the same field.
- [hard] REQ-03: The document names which operations belong on the trait versus derived helpers, with a worked GF(2)/GF(2^m) and GF(p)/GF(p^r) example each, and preallocates the module layout for the foundation tasks that follow.

planning.outcome: Relative-extension abstraction and algebraic field identity fixed by an approved design

terminal.consumer_family: foundation implementers consuming the extension design
terminal.test_boundary: documentation review against the linked investigation
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Single design document; no code changes

title: Implement the relative field-extension abstraction in gf2-core
description:
Implement the canonical relative finite-field extension abstraction designed for gf2-core, covering base-field embedding, checked membership and restriction, relative degree, relative Frobenius, field-order relationships, and reusable validation certificates.

## Background

The abstraction realizes the approved extension design. Existing pairs must be covered: GF(2) into runtime `Gf2mField`, and `ConstField` bases into the binomial towers. Validation work performed once (irreducibility, compatibility, order facts) is captured in a reusable certificate value so repeated constructions do not revalidate.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: gf2-core exposes the designed extension abstraction implemented for the existing binary and tower field pairs, with embedding, membership, restriction, relative degree, relative Frobenius, and order relationships behaving per the field-law conformance style of the crate.
- [hard] REQ-02: Validation certificates are constructed once, are reusable across constructions, and invalid pairs report typed errors from the core-owned error types.
- [hard] REQ-03: The shared field axiom/conformance harness gains extension-law cases exercised for the implemented pairs.

planning.outcome: gf2-core exposes the canonical relative extension abstraction with reusable validation certificates

terminal.test_boundary: extension-law conformance cases over the implemented pairs
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One trait surface with conformance coverage; design already fixed

title: Deterministic derivation of elements with exact multiplicative order
description:
Add the reusable gf2-core operation deriving an element of exact multiplicative order $n$ in an extension field, with deterministic canonical selection.

## Background

`Gf2mField::primitive_element` requires tables and there is no generic exact-order constructor. Non-primitive BCH lengths need an order-$n$ root of unity, and reproducibility requires that the same field and $n$ select the same element deterministically, not merely some element.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: gf2-core derives an element of exact multiplicative order $n$ for supported extension fields, validating the order exactly, with a documented deterministic canonical selection rule.
- [hard] REQ-02: A typed error reports the case where no order-$n$ element exists, and property tests cover order exactness plus selection determinism over binary and nonbinary fields.

planning.outcome: Exact-order elements derive deterministically for supported extension fields

terminal.test_boundary: order-exactness property tests spanning both field classes
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One algebraic operation with a deterministic selection rule

title: Minimal polynomials of extension elements over an arbitrary base field
description:
Add the reusable gf2-core operation computing the minimal polynomial of an extension element over an arbitrary base field through the extension abstraction.

## Background

The existing element operation is specialized to GF(2). General BCH generator assembly needs minimal polynomials over the actual base field; the operation belongs to the extension surface, not BCH-private code.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: gf2-core computes minimal polynomials of extension elements over an arbitrary base field, agreeing with the existing GF(2)-specialized operation on its domain.
- [hard] REQ-02: Property tests verify minimality, base-coefficient membership, and vanishing at the element plus its conjugates, over binary and nonbinary pairs.

planning.outcome: Minimal polynomials over arbitrary base fields are a reusable gf2-core operation

terminal.test_boundary: minimality property tests spanning both field classes
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One algebraic operation on an existing trait surface

title: Implement q-cyclotomic coset closure over extension fields
description:
Implement $q$-cyclotomic coset computation and seed-set closure in gf2-core: given a seed set of root exponents modulo $n$, derive the closed defining set under multiplication by $q$, partitioned into cosets.

## Background

General BCH construction accepts seed sets that are not already closed and derives the closure itself. Coset partitions also drive generator-polynomial assembly (one minimal polynomial per coset) and are a named Lean proof obligation, so the operation lives in gf2-core where the proof surface can reach it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: gf2-core computes the $q$-cyclotomic closure and coset partition of any seed set modulo $n$ with $\gcd(n,q)=1$, deterministically ordered.
- [hard] REQ-02: Property tests verify closure idempotence, coset disjointness, and agreement between coset unions and closure over binary and nonbinary cases.

planning.outcome: Seed sets close deterministically under q-cyclotomic conjugacy with coset partitions

terminal.test_boundary: coset-closure property tests
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One self-contained combinatorial-algebra operation

title: Generic irreducibility validation with reusable certificates
description:
Implement complete, eager irreducibility validation for polynomials over arbitrary supported finite fields, producing the reusable validation certificates the quotient fields consume.

## Background

Runtime quotient construction must fully validate its modulus; validation cost is paid once and captured in a certificate. The existing registry verifies binary irreducibility for specific entries; this operation is field-generic.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: gf2-core decides irreducibility for polynomials over supported base fields with a complete algorithm, returning a reusable certificate on success and a typed error naming a witness factor class on failure.
- [hard] REQ-02: Tests cover known irreducible and reducible cases over GF(2), GF(p), and GF(p^r) bases, within fast-tier budgets.

planning.outcome: Irreducibility validates completely with reusable certificates

terminal.test_boundary: irreducibility decision tests over the three base classes
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One decision algorithm with certificate output

title: Implement runtime-configured polynomial quotient extension fields
description:
Implement arbitrary-degree polynomial quotient extension fields in gf2-core with a runtime-configured modulus, defining the reference semantics of the pair.

## Background

The current tower types support only binomial moduli of degree two and three. The runtime form defines `quotient-extension-api`: representation, reduction, inversion, Frobenius, base embedding, and the algebraic field identity. Irreducibility validation and certificates come from the dedicated validation operation. Materialization beyond `usize`/`u128` limits returns a typed unsupported-size error.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A runtime quotient extension over supported base fields constructs from a certificate-validated modulus and satisfies the shared field-law conformance suite.
- [hard] REQ-02: The type implements the extension abstraction and carries the algebraic field identity fixed by the extension design.
- [hard] REQ-03: Materialization beyond `usize`/`u128` limits reports the typed unsupported-size error.

planning.outcome: Runtime polynomial quotient extensions construct with certificate-backed validation and stable identity

terminal.test_boundary: shared field-law conformance suite runs
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One field implementation over a finished validation layer

title: Implement compile-time configured quotient extensions with equivalence evidence
description:
Implement the compile-time configured form of arbitrary polynomial quotient extensions and demonstrate observable equivalence with the runtime form of the same field.

## Background

Performance-critical paths use compile-time configured fields in the style of the existing `ExtConfig` towers; exploratory use needs the runtime form. Both forms of the same field must be observably equivalent and share one algebraic field identity.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A compile-time configured quotient extension implements the same field and extension contracts as the runtime form and passes the shared field-law conformance suite.
- [hard] REQ-02: A shared differential suite shows observable equivalence between compile-time and runtime forms of representative fields, including identity equality.

planning.outcome: Compile-time quotient extensions match the runtime form observably

terminal.test_boundary: differential equivalence suite versus the runtime form
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Second implementation of an already-fixed contract with a differential harness

title: Automatic modulus selection: Conway registry plus deterministic verified search
description:
Extend the polynomial registry and automatic field construction so splitting-field moduli are selected deterministically: canonical Conway polynomials where they are defined and registered, and a documented deterministic verified irreducible-polynomial search otherwise.

## Background

The registry currently holds primitive entries for $m \le 16$, irreducibility-only entries for $m = 64..127$, and a single documented Conway-derived GF(2^32) entry; there is no deterministic verified search policy. Automatic construction must be reproducible across hosts and versions because serialized field identities depend on it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Automatic modulus selection is deterministic and documented: registry Conway entries are preferred where present, and the fallback search is a specified deterministic order with full irreducibility verification.
- [hard] REQ-02: Selection results are stable under repetition and covered by tests pinning representative selections, including at least one nonbinary base.
- [hard] REQ-03: Registry additions carry the same verification evidence style as existing entries.

planning.outcome: Automatic modulus selection is deterministic: Conway where defined, verified search otherwise

terminal.test_boundary: pinned deterministic-selection tests
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One selection policy over an existing registry

title: Design BchSpec, the code-trait generalization, and the compatibility boundary
description:
Author the design document fixing the canonical `BchSpec` model, the static-generic versus type-erased code type split, the field-generic block-code trait surface (including parity-check access), and the named, versioned compatibility boundary for code families that migrate later.

## Background

The planning brief fixes the semantic shape: `BchSpec` variants carrying only independent inputs, one `BchCode::construct` path, convenience constructors that delegate, and derived codes as generic wrappers. Today `BlockEncoder` is `BitVec`-bound, `GeneratorMatrixAccess` returns `BitMatrix`, and parity-check access is inherent per type, so the generic trait shape and the migration boundary must be fixed before construction or trait work fans out. The document also preallocates module layout for the trait, transform, and encoding tasks so parallel waves write disjoint files.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A design document fixes the `BchSpec` variant set with exact independent inputs, the construct/derivation pipeline stages, and the static/erased type split.
- [hard] REQ-02: The document fixes the field-generic block-code, encoder, generator-matrix, and parity-check trait surface with its `BitVec`/`BitMatrix` specializations, and names the compatibility boundary (name, version, removal condition) for unmigrated families.
- [hard] REQ-03: The document maps each current consumer family from the linked investigation inventory to immediate migration or the boundary, and preallocates the new module layout.

planning.outcome: BchSpec variants, generic trait surface, and compatibility boundary fixed by an approved design

terminal.consumer_family: epic implementation tasks consuming the design
terminal.test_boundary: documentation review against the investigation inventory
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Single design document synthesizing already-cited inventories

title: Introduce field-generic block-code traits with binary specializations
description:
Implement the designed field-generic block-code, encoding, generator-matrix, and parity-check trait surface with packed `BitVec`/`BitMatrix` binary specializations, and stand up the named compatibility boundary so existing code families compile unchanged.

## Background

This is the trait cutover child shared with the streaming/batch unification story: that story builds on these traits rather than designing a competing surface. Existing families (LDPC, CRC, product, GRAND consumers) remain on the compatibility boundary until their own migrations; BCH migrates within this epic.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The designed generic traits exist with binary specializations preserving packed behavior, and static generic implementations dispatch with zero-cost monomorphization.
- [hard] REQ-02: The named, versioned compatibility boundary keeps existing consumer families compiling and passing tests unchanged, with its removal condition recorded.
- [hard] REQ-03: Workspace tests, clippy with warnings denied, and formatting pass.

planning.outcome: Field-generic code traits exist with binary specializations and a named compatibility boundary

terminal.test_boundary: existing consumer suites unchanged with new trait conformance tests
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One trait surface with a shim; consumer migrations excluded

title: Implement the layered typed error surface for coding APIs
description:
Implement the coding-side typed error layers: general code/transform errors (invalid coordinates, buffer and shape mismatches, dynamic type mismatches) and the BCH construction/decoding errors that compose or wrap them.

## Background

Error ownership follows crate direction: gf2-core owns its field and matrix-IO error types; gf2-coding owns generic code and transform errors plus BCH-specific errors that wrap or compose the general layers. Generic APIs never expose BCH-specific types. Panics remain reserved for violated internal invariants.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A coding-general error layer covers transform coordinate errors, buffer/shape mismatches, and dynamic type mismatches, free of BCH-specific types.
- [hard] REQ-02: BCH construction and decoding errors are structured, carry the mathematically relevant context, compose the general layer where applicable, and are documented with their production conditions.

planning.outcome: A layered typed error surface spans the new coding-side boundaries

terminal.test_boundary: unit tests asserting each error's production condition
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One error-surface module with layered ownership

Add the type-erased/runtime code handle layer over the generic traits so exploratory workflows can hold heterogeneous codes without naming their field types.

## Success Criteria

title: Compact-until-requested matrices with caller buffers and opt-in caching
description:
Make generator and parity-check access compact by default: matrices are materialized only on request, into caller-provided buffers where asked, with caching an explicit opt-in.

## Background

The current BCH implementation caches its first computed `BitMatrix` unconditionally behind a mutex; the replacement access behavior applies to the new canonical code types, with the old cache deleted at cutover. Access is field-generic with packed binary specialization.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Generator and parity-check access provide allocating and caller-buffer materialization paths, field-generic with packed binary specialization, without implicit caching; shape mismatches report the coding-general error layer.
- [hard] REQ-02: Opt-in caching is explicit, documented, and covered by tests demonstrating both cached and uncached flows.

planning.outcome: Matrices stay compact until requested, with caller buffers and opt-in caching

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One access-behavior change on the new trait surface

title: Canonical checksummed FieldMatrix serialization with atomic replacement
description:
Implement the canonical serialization format for `FieldMatrix` carrying the algebraic field identity and a separately versioned element-representation header field, with checksummed payloads, atomic file replacement, and validated load-back, using core-owned IO error types.

## Background

The existing `.gf2` BitMatrix format has no checksum, non-atomic writes, and no field identity; its only production round trip is the LDPC cache and it stays untouched. The new format is field-generic, reuses the repository's atomic write-rename pattern and BLAKE3 integrity precedent, and deliberately carries no code-specific metadata. Errors are gf2-core IO types; coding-side errors never appear here.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Saving a `FieldMatrix` writes a versioned format carrying the algebraic field identity and the element-representation header with a checksummed payload, via write-temp, sync, atomic rename.
- [hard] REQ-02: Loading validates identity, representation, and checksum, returns the saved matrix losslessly, and reports any mismatch or corruption as a typed core-owned error.
- [hard] REQ-03: Round-trip and corruption tests cover binary and nonbinary fields, including a runtime/compile-time identity match case.

planning.outcome: FieldMatrix round-trips through a checksummed, atomic, identity-validated format

terminal.test_boundary: round-trip test suite with corruption coverage
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One serialization format with an existing atomicity/integrity pattern to reuse

title: Implement BchSpec and the consecutive-root construction path
description:
Implement the `BchSpec` model types and the canonical construction path for the consecutive-root flavors: primitive narrow-sense and primitive with arbitrary first root, over any supported base field.

## Background

Construction derives the generator polynomial from coset minimal polynomials via the public polynomial LCM, dimension $k$, a witnessed classical BCH bound from the longest consecutive root run, and the correction radius that bound implies; it validates $\gcd(n,q)=1$, exact root order, base/splitting-field compatibility, and coefficient restriction, reporting failures through the layered error surface. Remaining flavors (seed sets, explicit generators, non-primitive conventions, degenerate codes) land in the follow-on flavor task on this same pipeline.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `BchSpec` types exist per the approved design, and primitive consecutive-root specs construct through one path deriving generator, dimension, witnessed bound, and radius with the listed validations as typed errors.
- [hard] REQ-02: Binary primitive narrow-sense results agree with the current implementation's generator polynomials on representative parameters.
- [hard] REQ-03: Nonbinary primitive construction works over GF(p) and GF(p^r) bases with base-coefficient generators dividing $x^n-1$.

planning.outcome: Primitive consecutive-root BchSpecs construct through one validated, deriving path

terminal.test_boundary: construction property tests with legacy-agreement fixtures
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pipeline for one flavor family; further flavors split out

title: Complete the construction flavors: seed sets, explicit generators, non-primitive, boundary codes
description:
Extend the canonical construction path to the remaining `BchSpec` flavors: arbitrary seed sets with derived $q$-cyclotomic closure, explicitly supplied generator polynomials, non-primitive lengths with derived or explicit $n$-th roots of unity, and the mathematically valid boundary codes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Seed-set specs accept unclosed input, derive the closure, and construct with the witnessed bound from the longest consecutive run in the closed set.
- [hard] REQ-02: Explicit-generator specs verify splitting-field compatibility and $g(x) \mid x^n-1$, derive the root set, and reject incompatible generators with typed errors.
- [hard] REQ-03: Non-primitive lengths work with both the derived canonical order-$n$ element and an explicitly supplied root of unity, and the two agree when the explicit root is the canonical one.
- [hard] REQ-04: Empty seed sets yield the full-space code and complete defining sets yield the zero-dimensional code.

planning.outcome: Each remaining BchSpec flavor constructs through the same canonical path

terminal.test_boundary: flavor property tests over the closed construction pipeline
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Flavor extensions on a finished pipeline; no new pipeline stages

title: Add delegating convenience constructors with automatic field selection
description:
Add the ergonomic constructors (`primitive_narrow_sense`, `primitive`, defining-set, non-primitive forms) that build the corresponding `BchSpec` and delegate to the canonical path, accepting either an explicit splitting-field representation or automatic selection.

## Background

Constructors accept only independent mathematical inputs; derived quantities are validated on request, never supplied. Automatic selection uses the deterministic registry/search policy. The designed distance is presented as a guaranteed lower bound, never as the minimum distance.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each convenience constructor delegates to the canonical path, accepts only independent inputs, and supports explicit and automatic field selection.
- [hard] REQ-02: Doctests cover the concise binary primitive case deriving $(n, k, t)$ from the field and designed distance alone.

title: Generic shortening over arbitrary coordinate sets
description:
Implement shortening as a generic linear-code transformation over arbitrary coordinate sets: restrict to codewords zero on the chosen coordinates, delete them, derive the resulting dimension by rank, and report the resulting information-set structure.

## Background

Dimension follows from rank, not a count formula, and the result need not stay systematic in the original positions. Count-based helpers cover the conventional systematic positions. The rank/information-set machinery built here is shared by puncturing.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Shortening accepts arbitrary coordinate sets on any generic linear code, derives dimension by rank, reports the information-set structure, and preserves its coordinate map.
- [hard] REQ-02: Count-based helpers delegate to the coordinate-set form, and invalid coordinate sets report the coding-general error layer.
- [hard] REQ-03: Property tests verify dimension-by-rank against direct generator-matrix computation, including non-systematic cases, over binary and nonbinary codes.

planning.outcome: Arbitrary-coordinate shortening derives dimension by rank with provenance

title: General systematic BCH encoding across supported base fields
description:
Implement general BCH encoding over supported base fields with the canonical coordinate convention: coordinate $i \leftrightarrow x^i$ internally, `[message | parity]` as the default systematic user layout through an explicit zero-cost coordinate mapping, and declared standards-specific layouts.

title: Allocation-free single, workspace batch, and parallel batch encoding
description:
Add the performance-path encoding APIs: allocation-free single-codeword `encode_into`, reusable-workspace batch methods, and shared-parallel batch execution over supported worker counts, alongside the allocating conveniences.

## Background

The current batch encoder is a sequential map; large-batch throughput requires real multi-worker execution with deterministic ordered output and per-worker workspace partitioning, following the repository's parallel and determinism conventions.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-02: Batch encoding supports worker counts greater than one with deterministic, input-ordered output, workspace partitioning per worker, and identical results across supported worker counts.

title: Profile-driven dispatch among equivalent batch-encoding algorithms
description:
Implement the profile-driven selector dispatching among mathematically equivalent batch-encoding algorithm families, preserving at least one scalar reference encoder.

## Background

The dispatch mechanism is required; the concrete family set (polynomial remainder, precomputed linear recurrences, matrix-based kernels) follows the survey's workload-selection contract rather than being mandated up front. The selector composes with, and is distinct from, the SIMD feature-dispatch seam.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A dispatch seam selects among registered encoding algorithm families per profile, with the scalar reference always available and selected results bit-identical across families.
- [hard] REQ-02: At least two families are registered, chosen per the workload-selection contract, with differential tests proving equivalence on the predeclared corpus rows.

title: AVX2 batch-encoding kernels with complete feature detection and tested scalar fallback
description:
Implement AVX2 batch-encoding kernels for binary BCH through the existing carry-less-multiply primitives and function-pointer dispatch seam in gf2-kernels-simd, with a dispatch predicate covering the complete required ISA feature set and the scalar fallback exercised in tests.

## Background

The kernel crate already exposes PCLMULQDQ primitives, AVX2 detection, and safe function-pointer dispatch with scalar selection; the design compiles on the Rust 1.95 MSRV. Runtime safety requires detecting the full feature set the kernels use — carry-less multiply support in addition to AVX2 — as one combined predicate. Unsafe code stays isolated in the kernel crate.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: AVX2 batch encoding produces bit-identical results to the scalar reference on the predeclared corpus rows, including the packed word-boundary lengths 0, 1, 63, 64, and 65 with little-endian indexing and zero tail padding.
- [hard] REQ-02: The dispatch predicate detects the complete ISA feature set the kernels require before selecting them, and the scalar fallback path is exercised by tests independent of host capability.
- [hard] REQ-03: Kernel-crate unsafe carries safety contracts naming the detected features.

planning.outcome: AVX2 batch encoding is bit-identical to scalar with complete feature detection

title: Harden the binary decoder: canonical model, typed outcomes, verified corrections
description:
Migrate the binary BCH decoder to the canonical construction model and give it typed outcomes: `NoErrors`, `Corrected`, or `Uncorrectable`, where `Uncorrectable` means the bounded-distance procedure found no verified correction.

## Background

The current decoder returns flipped message bits without post-correction verification or failure reporting. The hardened decoder verifies candidate corrections by syndrome recomputation, documents the exact bounded-distance guarantee including possible beyond-radius miscorrection, and splits a no-allocation status/count fast path from an opt-in diagnostic path exposing corrected codeword, message, positions, and count. Nonbinary and derived-code decoding stay outside the epic.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The decoder consumes the canonical construction model and returns the typed outcome with candidate corrections verified before being reported as `Corrected`.
- [hard] REQ-02: The fast path corrects into caller storage returning status/count without allocation; the opt-in diagnostic path returns full structured evidence.
- [hard] REQ-03: The documented contract states the within-radius guarantee and beyond-radius miscorrection semantics in rustdoc, and error-injection tests cover all three outcomes at and beyond the radius.

planning.outcome: The binary decoder returns verified typed outcomes with fast and diagnostic paths

terminal.test_boundary: error-injection outcome tests around the radius
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One decoder result-contract migration; algorithms unchanged

title: Migrate HIP syndrome/decode support behaviorally intact
description:
Migrate the HIP GPU syndrome path and batch decode integration to the canonical construction model and typed decoder outcomes, preserving behavioral equivalence with the CPU path, with a committed HIP-host receipt.

## Background

The HIP path computes syndromes on device with BM/Chien/correction on CPU; existing byte-identity simulation tests pin CPU-versus-GPU agreement for the current status-less behavior and are the equivalence baseline for the migration.
